title: Implement deterministic backtest run manifests and strategy research metrics
description:
Implement the deterministic backtest runner and the immutable run manifest plus research metrics.

1. mike_trade/backtest/manifest.py: define RunManifest, a frozen dataclass/model.
   - Fields: run_id, created_at (UTC), config hash (a canonical, sorted-key hash of the effective config), symbols, window start/end, period role (RESEARCH, DEV or HOLDOUT), code revision (git commit plus a dirty flag, captured without network), data provenance/revision/vintage and dataset hash from the q.1 DataProvenance, starting capital, fee/slippage/fill/ambiguity assumptions, deterministic seed, and strategy names plus versions from the real strategy registry.
   - The manifest is written once and never mutated. A canonical serialization and content hash prove immutability, and rewriting an existing manifest raises.
   - Holdout protection:
     - A run tagged HOLDOUT requires an explicit holdout lock token/flag.
     - It records its access in the manifest.
     - It refuses a config whose hash differs from the locked research configuration, so retuning on a locked holdout is forbidden.
     - Research/dev windows that overlap the holdout window are rejected.

2. mike_trade/backtest/runner.py: implement BacktestRunner.
   - It wires the real strategy registry/classes, the session calendar, scheduler trigger semantics, budget/eligibility policies, position coordinator, cycle accounting and protection math to the q.1 ReplayClock/HistoricalReplayFeed and the q.2 HistoricalExecutionSimulator, using dependency injection only.
   - It replays strictly chronologically: evaluate strategies only on completed bars available as-of the clock, apply execution, and advance.
   - It must refuse any configuration that would construct a real broker client.
   - It persists durable trade/evaluation results per run: evaluations, signals, intents, fills, cycles and equity curve. Use the existing persistence journal/repositories where they fit; otherwise use a run-scoped results store keyed by run_id.
   - It runs only over an operator-supplied bounded window and symbol list (1-10 symbols). There is no implicit broad history download.

3. Metrics in runner.py, through a compute_metrics function over persisted results:
   - total and net return; cash and equity curve
   - per-trade P&L with entry/exit pairing, and hold duration
   - max drawdown, profit factor, win rate, average win/loss, expectancy net of costs
   - MFE/MAE (favorable/adverse excursion), using completed-bar data only within each holding window
   - breakdowns by symbol, month and time-of-day bucket in America/New_York
   - capital utilization
   - sample size with an uncertainty estimate: a deterministic seeded bootstrap CI for expectancy, plus a small-sample warning below a configured trade count

   Metrics never state or imply profitability beyond the computed numbers.

4. tests/unit/test_backtest_repro.py: synthetic, offline, no credentials. Cover:
   - identical manifest/results hash on rerun with the same inputs and seed
   - a different seed or config producing a different config hash/run_id
   - manifest immutability
   - holdout lock and anti-retuning rejection
   - hand-computed expected values on a small trade list for drawdown, profit factor, win rate, expectancy and MFE/MAE
   - refusal of real broker construction

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/backtest/clock.py, mike_trade/backtest/feed.py (q.1) and mike_trade/backtest/execution.py (q.2)
- mike_trade/strategies/registry.py, mike_trade/strategies/base.py, mike_trade/strategies/presets/pairs.py
- mike_trade/scheduling/scheduler.py, mike_trade/scheduling/triggers.py, mike_trade/scheduling/calendar.py
- mike_trade/execution/coordinator.py, mike_trade/portfolio/cycles.py, mike_trade/portfolio/budgets.py, mike_trade/risk/entry_eligibility.py
- mike_trade/persistence/journal.py, mike_trade/persistence/repositories.py, mike_trade/persistence/schema.py
- mike_trade/config/models.py (config canonicalization)

Decision budget: if a persistence schema change would be needed, use a run-scoped store inside the allowed files instead of adding migrations in this task. Document the choice in the module docstring.
acceptance_criteria: mike_trade/backtest/manifest.py defines an immutable RunManifest with config hash, symbols, window, period role, code revision, data provenance/revision/dataset hash, starting capital, fee/slippage/fill/ambiguity assumptions, seed and strategy versions
Writing a manifest for an existing run_id or modifying a persisted manifest raises; the canonical content hash is stable across serialize/deserialize

A HOLDOUT run without an explicit lock flag is rejected; a HOLDOUT run whose config hash differs from the locked research config is rejected; research/dev windows overlapping the holdout window are rejected

mike_trade/backtest/runner.py defines BacktestRunner, which resolves strategies through the real strategy registry (no hardcoded signal fixtures) and uses ReplayClock, HistoricalReplayFeed and HistoricalExecutionSimulator via injection
BacktestRunner raises before replay if any injected or configured broker resolves to a real Alpaca/paper/live client
Requests for more than 10 symbols or an unbounded/missing window are rejected
Two runs with identical dataset, config and seed produce byte-identical canonical results hashes; a test asserts this

compute_metrics returns total/net return, equity curve, per-trade P&L with entry/exit pairing, hold duration, max drawdown, profit factor, win rate, average win/loss, net expectancy, MFE/MAE, symbol/month/time-of-day breakdowns, utilization, sample size and a seeded bootstrap CI
Metric values on a hand-constructed trade list match hand-computed Decimal expectations in tests
A small-sample warning is emitted when the trade count is below the configured threshold
The modules import no Alpaca trading client, HTTP library or broker credential configuration
tests/unit/test_backtest_repro.py exists with positive and negative tests and passes when run alone
forbidden_changes: modify files outside allowed_write_paths, including q.1/q.2 backtest modules, strategy, scheduling, execution or persistence modules and migrations
change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
use hardcoded BUY/SELL fixtures in place of real registered strategy classes
inspect, evaluate or retune against a locked holdout window without the explicit lock flag
download historical data or construct any real broker client
use float for money, quantities or metric inputs where Decimal is required
create live broker orders or run broad test suites/backtests
